A 100 mW device in an 85 degC ambient sits at roughly TJ = 90 degC. **Conclusion for design: thermal resistance is not a limiting factor for a normally operating ATmega328P in the 28P3 PDIP.** The binding constraints in practice are the 200 mA total VCC/GND current limit, the 40 mA per-pin limit, the port-group current limits, and TA <= 85 degC (or <= 105 degC for -PN/-AN).

**Design targets to use in the absence of a datasheet Tj rating:** keep TJ below about 100-105 degC at worst-case ambient and worst-case dissipation (a conventional 20 degC derating below the 125 degC stress ceiling), and never treat 125 degC as an operating target. If the application is near the 0.3-0.8 W region implied above, the PDIP is the wrong package — move to the 32M1-A QFN, which has a exposed pad and a far lower theta-JA.

**On-die temperature sensing (for trend only).** The ATmega328P has an internal temperature sensor on ADC8 (MUX = 1000b, §24.9 'Temperature Measurement'). Its absolute accuracy is about plus/minus 10 degC and it is uncalibrated, so it is usable for relative trending and for detecting self-heating, not for verifying an absolute TJ. Do not use it to close a thermal budget.

## 5. Number register (so datasheet, derived and typical values are never mixed)

| Number | Meaning | Status |
|---|---|---|
| -55 degC to +125 degC | Absolute-maximum operating temperature | DATASHEET, §29.1 |
| -65 degC to +150 degC | Storage temperature | DATASHEET, §29.1 |
| 200 mA | DC current, VCC and GND pins | DATASHEET, §29.1 |
| 40 mA | DC current, per I/O pin / RESET / AVCC | DATASHEET, §29.1 |
| 6.0 V | Maximum operating voltage | DATASHEET, §29.1 |
| -40 to +85 degC / -40 to +105 degC | Guaranteed operating ambient (industrial / -AN,-PN codes) | DATASHEET, §29.2 and ordering table p. 627 |
| 1.10 W | 200 mA x 5.5 V current-limit-derived dissipation ceiling | DERIVED |
| 45-60 degC/W, 15-20 degC/W | theta-JA (still air, JEDEC 2-layer) and theta-JC, 28-lead 0.300 in PDIP | INDUSTRY-TYPICAL, not ATmega328P datasheet |
| 0.33-0.89 W, 0.40-2.22 W | Thermal-budget dissipation ceilings in the table in §4 | DERIVED from the assumed theta-JA above |

## 6. Verification checklist (about five minutes, against the actual PDF)

1. Open DS40002061B and go to the ATmega328P electrical-characteristics chapter, §29.1 'Absolute Maximum Ratings' (p. 308 in the 09/2020 printing).
2. Confirm the bulleted list matches §1 above, and confirm there is no row containing 'thermal', 'junction', 'dissipation' or a theta symbol.
3. Full-document search for 'thermal', 'theta', 'junction', 'dissipation'. Expect hits only on the typical-characteristic graphs (temperature-labelled curves) and the ordering/package pages — no ratings table.
4. Confirm package code 28P3 = 28-lead, 0.300 in PDIP in the ordering table (p. 627) and that §39 contains only mechanical drawings for 32A, 28M1, 32M1-A and 28P3.
5. If a customer or QA record requires a theta-JA, raise the request against package code 28P3 as described in §3 rather than back-filling a number from a secondary source.

## 7. Direct answers as they should be recorded

- Ask 2 (theta-JA, ATmega328P, 28-pin PDIP, DS40002061B 09/2020): **not specified in the datasheet.** No value exists in the cited source; blocked.
- Ask 3 (maximum junction temperature or total power dissipation specified by the datasheet): **none specified.** The nearest stated limits are the absolute-maximum operating temperature of -55 degC to +125 degC, the guaranteed operating ambient of -40 to +85 degC (-40 to +105 degC for -AN/-PN), and the 200 mA / 40 mA current ceilings of §29.1.

verdict.summary:
IRF540NPbF (Infineon, Rev. 2.1, 2026-07-24) — maximum power dissipation and linear derating

1. SOURCE AND DOCUMENT IDENTITY
Document: Infineon IRF540NPbF datasheet, page 1, 'Absolute Maximum Rating' table. Revision footer on every page reads 'Rev. 2.1, 2026-07-24'; Revision History (p.9) confirms '2026-07-24 / 2.1 — Update datasheet to Infineon format; Updated Package Outline and Part marking – page 8; Added disclaimer on last page.' Mirrors fetched (all sha256 a3fd62a76cc8, i.e. byte-identical):
  - https://www.infineon.com/dgdl/Infineon-IRF540N-DataSheet-v01_01-EN.pdf
  - https://www.infineon.com/dgdl/irf540npbf.pdf?fileId=5546d462533600a4015355e39f0d19a1
  - https://www.infineon.com/assets/row/public/documents/24/49/infineon-irf540n-datasheet-en.pdf
  - https://www.infineon.com/dgdl/Infineon-IRF540N-DataSheet-v01_01-EN.pdf?fileId=5546d462533600a4015355e34cf42335
The revision matches the one named in the question, so no revision-substitution caveat applies.

2. VERBATIM EXTRACT (page 1, Absolute Maximum Rating)
  ID @ TC = 25 degC, Continuous Drain Current, VGS @ 10 V ......... 33 A
  ID @ TC = 100 degC, Continuous Drain Current, VGS @ 10 V ........ 23 A
  IDM Pulsed Drain Current ....................................... 110 A
  PD @ TC = 25 degC  Maximum Power Dissipation ................... 130 W
  Linear Derating Factor ......................................... 0.87 W/degC
  VGS Gate-to-Source Voltage ..................................... +/- 20 V
  TJ Operating Junction and Storage Temperature Range ............ -55 to +175 degC
  (Thermal Resistance table) RthJC Junction-to-Case ............. max 1.15 degC/W
                              RthCS Case-to-Sink, flat greased ... typ 0.50 degC/W
                              RthJA Junction-to-Ambient .......... max 62 degC/W
Note the symbol is explicitly 'PD @ TC = 25 degC' — the rating is referenced to CASE temperature, not ambient. The Ta-referenced number in this datasheet is RthJA = 62 degC/W (free-air, no heatsink), which is a different quantity and is not the value asked for.

3. ANSWERS
(1) Maximum power dissipation at Tc = 25 degC: PD = 130 W.
(2) Linear derating factor: 0.87 W/degC (equivalently 0.87 W per degC of case-temperature rise above 25 degC).
(3) Maximum power dissipation permitted at Tc = 100 degC:
      PD(100) = PD(25) - (derating factor) x (100 - 25)
              = 130 W - 0.87 W/degC x 75 degC
              = 130 W - 65.25 W
              = 64.75 W
    Rounded to one decimal: 64.8 W. To the nearest watt: 65 W.
    Recommended reporting: 64.75 W (64.8 W at the datasheet's own two-significant-figure precision on the derating factor).

4. CROSS-CHECKS (all performed; none contradict the stated values)
 a) Derating factor vs. thermal resistance: the derating slope must equal 1/RthJC. 1 / 1.15 degC/W = 0.8696 W/degC, which rounds to the tabulated 0.87 W/degC. Agrees.
 b) PD(25) vs. Tjmax: PD(25) = (Tjmax - 25)/RthJC = (175 - 25)/1.15 = 130.4 W -> tabulated 130 W. Agrees (the 130 W is the silicon-limited rating set by RthJC and Tjmax = 175 degC, not a package limit).
 c) PD(100) via thermal resistance: (175 - 100)/1.15 = 65.2 W. This is 0.47 W (0.7%) above the 64.75 W from the tabulated rounded derating factor; the difference is entirely the rounding of 0.8696 to 0.87. Both land on 'about 65 W'. The 64.75 W figure is the one the question asks for, because it is derived from the two tabulated numbers requested.
 d) Junction-temperature closure: 100 degC + 64.75 W x 1.15 degC/W = 174.5 degC, i.e. just inside the 175 degC Tj limit. Consistent by construction; confirms 64.75 W is a real ceiling and not an extrapolation beyond the valid range.
 e) Current-rating consistency at 100 degC: the table gives ID = 23 A at Tc = 100 degC. Implied allowed Rds(on) = PD/ID^2 = 64.75/23^2 = 0.122 ohm, a plausible hot Rds(on) for this die at Tj near 175 degC. At 25 degC, 130/33^2 = 0.119 ohm. The two current ratings are consistent with the same power envelope, so the power numbers are internally coherent.
 f) Linearity assumption: the datasheet states a single 'Linear Derating Factor' and provides Fig. 9 (Maximum Drain Current vs. Case Temperature) and Fig. 11 (transient thermal impedance); no breakpoint or piecewise derating is declared for the 25-100 degC span in the absolute-maximum table, and the 25 degC point and the Tjmax intercept close the line exactly. A single-slope derating from 25 degC to Tjmax is therefore the datasheet's own model. If a graph-read of Fig. 9 is used instead, expect ~1-2% deviation from 23 A-equivalent power, not a different regime.

5. DESIGN NOTES / CAVEATS FOR USE OF THESE NUMBERS
 - Tc = 25 degC is a case temperature, i.e. it presumes an ideal heat sink holding the tabulation point at 25 degC. It is not achievable without a heat sink, and it is not the ambient-referenced rating (which would use RthJA = 62 degC/W, giving 130 W only at an impossible Ta). Any real design must add RthCS = 0.50 degC/W (flat, greased) plus the heat-sink-to-ambient resistance, and re-derive PD = (Tjmax - Tambient)/(RthJC + RthCS + RthSA) with margin on Tjmax.
 - The datasheet's own front-page text states the TO-220 package is used 'at power dissipation levels to approximately 50 watts'. The 130 W / 64.75 W numbers are silicon-limited (junction-to-case) and are not a statement that the package leads, tab, or mould compound will survive 65 W continuously. For continuous operation above roughly 50 W, treat the package/lead-frame and the solder-joint/PCB copper spreading as the binding constraint and verify with the transient thermal impedance (Fig. 11) plus a physical thermal test.
 - Infineon's public product page for IRF540N (fetched same session) lists Ptot max = 140 W and RthJC max = 1.1 K/W. That is a different parametric dataset (legacy IRF540N characterization) and does not match the Rev. 2.1 datasheet's 130 W / 1.15 degC/W. For this question the datasheet governs; if a BOM or thermal model is being built, use 130 W / 0.87 W/degC / 1.15 degC/W and note the web-page discrepancy in the design record.
 - Precision convention used and recommended: carry 64.75 W through the calculation, report 64.8 W (one decimal, matching the two-decimal input 0.87) or 65 W (nearest watt). Do not report 64.75 W as if it had four-figure accuracy; the underlying derating factor is only two significant figures.
